purpose: The supervisor keeps delivering when GitHub limits the account, and a stopped supervisor comes back and is visible instead of silently idle.

authorization.grantedBy: owner (netbka), delegated to the owner's main session
authorization.text: On 2026-10-12 the owner directed: "take this as starting point and deliver till end. Delivery this work with the AIWorks environment." The starting point is docs/PROJECT_WORKSPACE_PLAN.md (PR #12), with owner decisions D1, D3, D5 (direction only) and D9 recorded in its section 8. This campaign fixes problems the monitoring session found while running phase 1: publication through the REST API instead of GraphQL (#21) and a supervisor that restarts itself and shows when it stopped (#18). Commits are published as PRs only: the supervisor never merges or deploys, and the live runtime, its data directory, the governance checkout and the scheduled tasks are never touched. No run cap or cost ceiling (AW-002); provider limits are waited out. Provider order Claude, then Codex.

constraints: Program netbka/aiworks#14: deliver docs/PROJECT_WORKSPACE_PLAN.md through supervisor campaigns. Change only the files your task names. Other campaigns change other files at the same time: never edit their files, other agents' branches or worktrees, or campaigns/*.json.

Your assigned worktree is the only place you change files. Never touch D:/Git/aiworks/.local (live runtime, supervisor data directory, governance checkout, other worktrees) or the main checkout, and never start, stop or restart the supervisor, its scheduled tasks or the dashboard.

No production access, deployment, GitHub Actions changes, paid services, Telegram or other provider API calls, or new recurring spend. Never read .env contents, credentials or secret files. Read Engineering Platform only with read-only gh commands; never write the governance checkout or open changes in another repository: EP-side changes are proposed as text.
Follow AGENTS.md: run npm ci once in your worktree, then npm run check after changes. Report exact commands and pass/fail tallies.

Never weaken an assertion, delete or skip a test, or broaden a timeout to make the gate pass. Tests make no model, network or GitHub calls: synthetic executables and disposable git repositories, as tests/supervisor/helpers.mjs does.

Keep AW-001 to AW-007 as written. Do not enable a power whose decision is still open (GitHub-free local admission, Auto Release, Telegram delivery): design it, or build it switched off, and name the decision it waits for.

Label every claim about the running system observed, verified, planned or unknown (AGENTS.md evidence rule); merged is not deployed. Do not comment on GitHub, merge, close issues or change labels: the supervisor publishes your verified commit. Write "Refs #N", never "Closes".
Write for the owner first: plain English, short sentences, the outcome before the mechanism. Link Engineering Platform policies instead of copying them.

tasks.title: Publish through the GitHub REST API instead of GraphQL
tasks.outcome: A verified result is published even when the account's GraphQL quota is used up, and a rate limit waits exactly until GitHub's reset.
tasks.goal: Fix #21 (gh issue view 21). In src/supervisor/adapters/github.mjs replace the GraphQL-backed gh pr list, gh pr create and gh pr view calls with REST calls through gh api: GET repos/{repo}/pulls?head={owner}:{branch}&state=open for the lookup, POST repos/{repo}/pulls to create, GET repos/{repo}/pulls/{n} for the merge receipt (merged, merge_commit_sha, head.sha, base.ref). Keep the lookup-before-create reconciliation and the exact URL, head and base checks of integratedPullRequest unchanged. When GitHub refuses a call for a rate limit, record its reset time (x-ratelimit-reset, retry-after) and wait until then instead of the fixed publishRetryMs; other failures keep today's retry. Extend the synthetic gh in tests/supervisor/helpers.mjs to answer these REST routes and to simulate a rate-limit refusal with a reset time. Update docs/SUPERVISOR.md where it names the GitHub calls.
constraints: Change only src/supervisor/adapters/github.mjs, the publish retry path in src/supervisor/controller.mjs, tests/supervisor/** and docs/SUPERVISOR.md. No new dependency, token or credential handling: gh api keeps using the owner's existing gh login.
acceptance: No supervisor code path calls gh pr list, gh pr create, gh pr view or any GraphQL endpoint; a test with a synthetic gh fails if one is called.
Publication, the crash-between-push-and-PR reconciliation and the merge-receipt integration check pass with the REST routes (existing tests unchanged, plus a REST-specific case).
A rate-limit refusal with a reset time makes the task wait until that reset (plus a small margin) and then publish once; no duplicate PR (tested).
npm run check passes; the PR states nothing is deployed.

tasks.title: A stopped supervisor restarts itself and says that it stopped
tasks.outcome: If the supervisor process dies, it is running again within minutes, and anyone looking sees when and why it stopped.
tasks.goal: Fix #18 (gh issue view 18). On 2026-10-12 the AIWorks Supervisor task ended with 0xC000013A (console control exit) and stayed down: keep restarts serve, but nothing restarts keep, and Task Scheduler does not treat that exit as a failure. (1) In scripts/supervisor/install-windows-task.ps1 and install-dashboard-task.ps1 add a repeating trigger (every 5 minutes, indefinitely) next to the logon trigger, with MultipleInstances IgnoreNew, so a dead keeper or dashboard is started again; keep the existing STOP-file protocol of scripts/supervisor/deploy.ps1 working (a deploy in progress must not be undone by the repeating trigger: check how deploy.ps1 stops and starts the tasks and keep it correct). (2) keep logs why it ends (signal, exit code) to supervisor.log before it exits. (3) status and the store-reading dashboard API report "supervisor stopped" with the time of the last lease renewal when every lease has expired, so the owner view can lead with it. Document the behaviour in docs/SUPERVISOR.md section 6 and README.md.
constraints: Change only scripts/supervisor/*.ps1, src/supervisor/cli.mjs, src/supervisor/api.mjs, the store-reading part of src/dashboard (not its pages beyond one plain status line), tests/** and docs/SUPERVISOR.md and README.md. Never install, register or change the live scheduled tasks yourself; the scripts are applied by the operator through the upgrade procedure.
acceptance: The task scripts register a repeating trigger with MultipleInstances IgnoreNew for both tasks; a test or script check shows the generated task definition, and deploy.ps1 still stops and restarts cleanly with the STOP file (reasoned in the PR with the exact order of operations).
keep writes its exit reason to the log before ending (tested with a synthetic child).
status reports the supervisor as stopped, with the last lease renewal time, when every lease has expired (tested); a live controller is never reported stopped.
npm run check passes; the PR lists the operator steps to apply the new task definitions through the upgrade procedure.
